punchline: Howard Schultz came back from Milan certain that an espresso bar sells company as much as coffee, while Starbucks was selling only beans.
thirty_sec: In 1983 Howard Schultz visited Milan and noticed that espresso bars were places where people met, not just bought coffee. Starbucks was then selling only beans. He pushed for espresso drinks, the founders hesitated, and he got a small trial in one corner of a Seattle store. They still declined to expand, so he left to start Il Giornale.
